property_summary: A call to setL1BlockValues by a caller other than the depositor reverts in the original contract.
Any account other than the depositor must not be able to execute setL1BlockValues successfully.
After any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the number getter must return the _number argument passed in the call; the mutant fails this because it never updates number.
After any call to setL1BlockValues, the value of number must equal the _number argument passed; the buggy version always sets it to 0, violating this for any non-zero _number.
After setL1BlockValues, number must equal the _number argument, but the bug sets number to _timestamp instead.
A call to setL1BlockValues from a non-depositor account must revert.
A call to setL1BlockValues must revert unless the caller is the depositor account

After any call to setL1BlockValues, the timestamp state variable must equal the input _timestamp parameter. The buggy version omits this assignment, leaving timestamp unchanged from its previous value.
After calling setL1BlockValues, timestamp must equal the _timestamp argument; the bug sets it to _number, so the invariant breaks when _timestamp != _number.
After any call to setL1BlockValues, the basefee stored in the contract must equal the _basefee argument passed to that call. The mutant breaks this by adding 1, so basefee != _basefee.
The reference contract always updates basefee to the provided _basefee value after setL1BlockValues is called, while the mutant leaves basefee unchanged.
hash can be changed only once, when set alongside a new sequenceNumber by the depositor; any subsequent call that changes hash must revert.
Setting L1 block values reverts for any caller that is not the depositor account.
For callers other than the depositor account, the call to setL1BlockValues must revert; for the depositor, it must succeed.
After setL1BlockValues is called, the hash state variable must equal the _hash argument passed; the buggy version can leave hash unchanged when _hash differs from its previous value.
The state variable hash must equal the _hash argument passed to setL1BlockValues when called by the depositor; the buggy version always sets hash to zero, violating this rule for any non-zero _hash.
The hash state variable must equal the last _hash argument passed to setL1BlockValues; the mutant breaks this because it stores keccak256(abi.encodePacked(_hash)) instead of the raw _hash.
After any call to setL1BlockValues, the stored sequenceNumber must equal the provided _sequenceNumber argument; the bug retains the old value, violating equality.

In setL1BlockValues, the stored sequenceNumber must equal the _sequenceNumber argument passed by the caller; the mutant stores a value derived from _batcherHash instead, violating this invariant when the arguments differ.
After setL1BlockValues is called, c.sequenceNumber() must equal the _sequenceNumber argument passed; the buggy version violates this by setting sequenceNumber to _timestamp instead.

After any call to setL1BlockValues with any inputs, the batcherHash state variable must equal the _batcherHash argument; the mutant fails this because it does not assign batcherHash, so the stored value equals its previous value instead of the new argument.
After a call to setL1BlockValues, the batcherHash state variable must equal the _batcherHash argument provided, but the buggy version incorrectly sets it to _hash.

After a successful call to setL1BlockValues, batcherHash should equal the provided _batcherHash argument; the buggy modifier always reverts, so the transaction fails and batcherHash retains its prior value instead of updating.

After a successful call to setL1BlockValues, the stored batcherHash must equal the provided _batcherHash argument; the buggy modifier always reverts so a successful call is impossible, yet after a pranked call from the depositor the reference updates batcherHash correctly while the mutant leaves it unchanged.
